why: `e as T` checks nothing at run time (the emit drops it), and neither does an any or unknown value filling a typed slot. The proof lane read such a value as an uninterpreted conversion into T and then read T's operations exactly, so `x as number` on a string | number, `x as string` on unknown, `JSON.parse(s) as { a: number }` and an any parameter in a number local were each proved equal to a candidate adding 0 or "" ("a" + 0 is "a0"). Now the value is read with its real type (common.mjs assertionHeld): the opaque Any for an any or unknown source or a source mixing types, the source's own type for one primitive family. `v + 0` is then an uninterpreted operation on Any and differs from `v`: the four are not proved, lane B witnesses each. widen (to a supertype), rank (a literal into its union), bump (a number asserted to a literal union, read as the number) and twice (the same operation on an opaque value on both sides) are proved beside plain.
